;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018–19 Sudanese protests]], [[2019 Sudanese coup d'état]]
**The [[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese military]] surrounds the [[presidential palace]] in the capital [[Khartoum]], and takes over state media buildings amid protests against [[President of Sudan|President]] [[Omar al-Bashir]]. Several senior ministers are reportedly arrested, including former Defense Minister [[Abdel Rahim Mohammed Hussein]]. [https://www.thenational.ae/world/africa/army-poised-to-take-power-in-sudan-after-mass-protests-against-president-omar-al-bashir-latest-1.847537 (''The National'')]
**The army forms an [[Transitional Military Council (2019)|interim council]], with [[Vice President of Sudan#First Vice Presidents|First Vice President]] Lt. General [[Ahmed Awad Ibn Auf]] as the leader. President al-Bashir is reported to have stepped down. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-47891470 (BBC News)]
;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Australian federal election]]
**[[Prime Minister of Australia|Australian Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] calls an election for 18 May. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-04-11/federal-election-live-scott-morrison-calls-may-18-election-date/10968588 (ABC News Australia)]
*[[North Korea]] appoints [[Choe Ryong-hae]] as President of the Presidium of the [[Supreme People's Assembly]], the country's nominal head of state, replacing [[Kim Yong-nam]] after 21 years. [[Kim Jae-ryong]] becomes [[Premier of North Korea|premier]]. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20190412001351325 (Yonhap)]

;Law and crime
*[[Abortion in South Korea]]
**The [[Constitutional Court of Korea]] rules that the 1953 [[abortion]] ban is unconstitutional. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20190411000679 (''Korea Herald'')]
*[[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] is arrested in [[London]] after [[Ecuador]] withdraws [[Right of asylum|asylum]]. He is later found guilty of breaching bail in 2012 by a British court, however he faces likely [[extradition]] to the United States over allegations he conspired with former US military analyst [[Chelsea Manning]] to acquire classified U.S. government files. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/live/2019/apr/11/wikileaks-founder-julian-assange-arrested-at-the-ecuadorean-embassy-live-updates (''The Guardian'')]
*Police in Louisiana arrest Holden Matthews, a suspect in arson at three historically [[African-American church]]es in the past weeks which the [[NAACP]] flagged as hate crimes. Matthews is the son of a local deputy sheriff. He has ties to [[black metal]] music and commented on memes about musician [[Varg Vikernes]], a neo-Nazi who boasted about burning churches in Norway and was imprisoned for arson and murder, but researchers are unsure if they prove hate was his motive. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/black-church-fires-louisiana-suspect-holden-matthews-charged/ (CBS)] [https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/holden-matthews-varg-wikernes-norwegian-black-metal-lords-of-chaos-820995/ (''Rolling Stone'')] [https://www.thedailybeast.com/holden-matthews-arrested-in-string-of-louisiana-church-fires (Daily Beast)]
*[[Michael Avenatti]] is charged by a [[Grand juries in the United States#Federal law|federal grand jury]] in [[California]] on 36 counts, including [[embezzlement]], [[Mail and wire fraud#Wire|wire fraud]], [[tax evasion]], [[Bankruptcy#Fraud|bankruptcy fraud]] and [[bank fraud]] connected to his alleged [[theft]] of tens of millions of dollars from several clients. [https://www.justice.gov/usao-cdca/pr/attorney-michael-avenatti-named-federal-grand-jury-indictment-accuses-him-stealing (United States Department of Justice)] [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/feds-file-charges-michael-avenatti/story?id=62329205 (ABC News)]
;Science and technology
*[[Israel]]'s ''[[Beresheet]]'' [[lunar lander]] crashes at [[Mare Serenitatis]] on the surface of the [[Moon]]. The crash resulted from a failure in the lander's main engine, resulting in the total loss of the spacecraft. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/11/science/israel-moon-landing-beresheet.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[SpaceX]]'s [[Falcon Heavy]] launches successfully from [[Kennedy Space Center]] carrying [[Arabsat-6A]] to orbit. All three boosters landed successfully, marking the first time that all three boosters of a Falcon Heavy landed without failure. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/04/11/tech/spacex-falcon-heavy-arabsat-launch/index.html (''CNN'')]
